economy.summary: Voted in June 2023 for House Bill 1500, which would raise Pennsylvania's minimum wage; the bill passed the House 103-100.
economy.short: Voted for bill to raise Pennsylvania's minimum wage.

taxes.summary: Voted in June 2023 for House Bill 1100, which expanded the state's Property Tax/Rent Rebate program and supplemental tax reduction for older adults and people with disabilities; the bill passed the House 194-9 and later became law.
taxes.short: Voted to expand Property Tax/Rent Rebate program.

abortion.summary: In July 2022 voted against Senate Bill 106, a package of proposed constitutional amendments that included language stating the Pennsylvania Constitution does not grant any right relating to abortion, including taxpayer-funded abortion; the package also covered election-related provisions.
abortion.short: Voted against amendment package declaring no constitutional abortion right.

education.summary: Announced state Competitive Equipment Grants for career and technical education programs at Erie schools in June 2026, saying students learn best in classrooms where they can learn by doing; this is a funding announcement rather than a campaign platform.
education.short: Announces CTE equipment grants; backs hands-on career education.

healthcare.summary: Sponsored House Bill 1961 to have Pennsylvania join a multistate licensure compact for physician assistants, which he said would streamline licensing across state lines and expand telehealth services; the bill passed the House in November 2025.
healthcare.short: Sponsored physician-assistant licensure compact bill expanding telehealth services.

energy.summary: Announced a $25,000 state grant in June 2026 to plan solar panels and a green roof on Erie's municipal building, saying investing in energy efficiency and clean power is smart for taxpayers and the environment; this is a funding announcement rather than a campaign platform.
energy.short: Announces solar planning grant; calls clean-power investment smart.

guns.summary: Voted in May 2023 for House Bill 714, which would require background checks on all firearm sales in Pennsylvania, including private sales; the bill passed the House 109-92.
guns.short: Voted for universal firearm background checks bill.
